experiment: PX-5 (rtx-11): cudaGraph capture of the prefill chunk loop (short-ctx TTFT)
gpu: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition, 97887 MiB, single GPU (sm_120a / cc 12.0, 188 SMs)
verdict: NO-GO — do NOT build. The maximum possible TTFT saving is < 0.03% of short-ctx TTFT, ~70-100x below the ~2% go threshold. Recorded by the go/no-go arithmetic below; graph capture/replay was NOT implemented.

go_no_go_arithmetic.premise_check: The plan hypothesised 'short ctx / many small chunks'. FALSE for plow's bucket ladder. The prefill chunk loop (gemma4_sm120_chat.cu) picks the SMALLEST bucket >= remaining tokens from [128,512,1024,2048,4096,8192] (MAX_CHUNK=8192). So ANY prompt <= 8192 tokens is a SINGLE prefill chunk = a SINGLE cooperative launch. 'Many small chunks' never occurs at short ctx; multi-launch only begins ABOVE 8192 tokens (LONG ctx), where TTFT is seconds and any per-launch tax is even more negligible. There is NO context regime where a chunk-loop graph is material.

measured_inputs.chunks_at_short_ctx: 1 (512-tok prompt: one 512 bucket; 2048-tok prompt: one 2048 bucket) — confirmed from the harness run ('512 tokens in 415.9 ms', single PREFILL line)
measured_inputs.per_token_host_prologue_us: 44 (measured on THIS box, gemma4_sm120_chat decode host-prologue breakdown: 0.044 ms/step = kv-row patch + 3 scalars + counter zero + launch; matches the plan's cited 53 us)
measured_inputs.prefill_chunk_host_prologue_us_upper_bou: ~80 (the decode 44 us plus the full instruction-stream cudaMemcpy which a single prefill chunk uploads; still same order)

ceiling_computation.removable_by_graph: The counter zeroing (cudaMemset) and kv-row patch (cudaMemcpy) become graph nodes and the cooperative launch becomes a graph node — a graph replay removes the HOST-SIDE issue cost of these per chunk, NOT the device compute. At 1 chunk that is at most ONE prefill host prologue (<= ~80 us).
ceiling_computation.margin: the ceiling is ~70-400x below the go threshold at every short-ctx point

measurements.harness: gemma4_sm120_chat (rt-build, /root/gpu-assets), PLOW_PREFILL=1 PLOW_UNISEG=1, gemma4-12b-ctx4096-uniseg.pkt, checkpoint gemma-4-12B-it, prompts truncated from prompt_tpot.ids, n_gen=20 (to also emit the decode host/device breakdown).
measurements.note: prefill_ms values are the rt-build first-cut prefill object (older than the T5 perf-data numbers); the ABSOLUTE ms differ from perf-data/gemma4-12b-plow-prefill-sm120.md but that is irrelevant to the ratio — TTFT is hundreds-to-thousands of ms and the removable host overhead is tens of us, so the ceiling is negligible for any prefill object. The decode breakdown (host 0.044 ms vs launch+sync 18.07 ms) independently shows host issue is 0.24% of even a single decode step; a prefill chunk's kernel is far larger, so its host fraction is smaller still.

why_not_built: cudaGraph capture/replay of the chunk sequence would add real complexity (per-chunk graph node param updates for the counter-zero memset and the kv-row-patch memcpy, plus re-capture when the bucket shape changes) for a saving bounded above at 0.02% of TTFT. This matches the plan's own note ('the per-token host prologue is already 53 us, so the ceiling here is small') and the T9c finding ('host enqueue tax 3.08 us/launch — negligible vs the ~514 ms GEMM-bound compute'). The prefill wall is GEMM/flash compute, not host launch overhead; PX-1 (batched prefill) and PX-2 (fp8 mainloop) attack that wall, PX-5 does not.
